C-6.Name: Fix active-tab visibility: auto-scroll the tab strip to the active tab
C-6.Summary: editorWithTabs/tabs.vue highlights the active tab (li.active) but never scrolls the tab strip. The strip scrolls only manually (wheel/trackpad handleTabScroll, drag autoscroll), so whenever activation changes without a direct click — Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycling (tabs.cycleForward / tabs.cycleBackward), sidebar tree / search / opened-files selection, close-to-neighbor activation, session restore — the active tab can remain outside the visible window of .scrollable-tabs. With overflow hidden and no scrollbar the visible strip then gives zero indication which tab is active. Fix: watch currentFile.id plus the tab id order and apply the minimal scrollLeft adjustment that fully reveals the active tab; also run once after mount so a restored session starts with the active tab visible.

Problem.Description: The active tab is not brought into view when activation changes programmatically; the user cannot tell which tab is active when it sits off-screen.
Problem.RootCause: tabs.vue has no logic tying currentFile changes to tabContainer scrollLeft; handleTabScroll (wheel) is the only scroll path and the drag autoscroll only runs mid-drag.
Problem.Evidence: grep scrollIntoView across src/renderer/src/components → only commandPalette/index.vue; no write to tabContainer.scrollLeft outside handleTabScroll. Activation call sites that bypass the strip: commands/index.js tabs.cycleForward/Backward (bus mt::tabs-cycle-*), sideBar/treeFile.vue, sideBar/treeOpenedTab.vue, sideBar/searchResultItem.vue, store/project.js session restore, and CLOSE_TAB neighbor activation.

Goals.R-1: Pure geometry helper computeActiveTabScroll({ activeLeft, activeWidth, scrollLeft, viewportWidth }) in src/renderer/src/util/tabsScroll.js: returns the minimal scrollLeft that fully reveals the tab (clamped at 0), or null when the tab is already fully visible. No DOM access, so it is unit-testable in jsdom.
Goals.R-2: tabs.vue scrollActiveTabIntoView(): read li[data-id=<currentFile.id>]:not(.gu-mirror) offsetLeft/offsetWidth against tabContainer scrollLeft/clientWidth, apply the helper result. Triggered by (a) a watcher whose source is the primitive join of currentFile.id + the tabs id order (Object.is dedup: an array-returning getter would fire on every tracked re-run), (b) once after mount, and (c) a watcher on layout showTabBar flipping true (display:none discards scrollLeft, so re-showing the hidden bar must re-reveal the active tab). The id-order source covers dragula reorder and add/remove that move the active tab while its id stays the same.
Goals.R-3: Manual wheel scrolling is untouched; when the active tab is already fully visible no scroll happens (helper returns null).
Goals.R-4: Unit tests in tests/renderer/components/tabs-scroll.test.js: all helper branches (left clip, right clip, already visible, clamp at 0, wider-than-viewport left-align + idempotence) plus component integration (switch to right-side tab scrolls, switch to left-side tab scrolls back, visible switch is a no-op, array-replacement reorder and real in-place EXCHANGE_TABS_BY_ID splice reorder with unchanged active id scroll, same-id clone replacement of currentFile does not re-scroll, ghost active id is a silent no-op, initial mount scrolls, re-showing the hidden tab bar scrolls).

Constraints.Constraint: Do not use Element.scrollIntoView: it can scroll ancestor containers and is uncontrollable in jsdom; compute scrollLeft manually against .scrollable-tabs only.

jsdom has no layout: offsetLeft/offsetWidth/clientWidth are stubbed in tests via Object.defineProperty; the production code path stays layout-read only, never triggering reflow writes beyond scrollLeft.
No dragula interference: select the tab by data-id, not by the .active class, so a gu-mirror clone during an active drag can never be the scroll target.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Edge fade / overflow indicators or a visible scrollbar for the strip (separate UX decision); smooth scroll animation.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: After any activation change (cycle, sidebar, close-neighbor, reorder, restore) the active tab ends fully inside the visible window of the strip, clamped to [0, scrollWidth - clientWidth].
Clicking a visible tab or re-activating the current tab causes no scroll jump.
Renderer suites green; new tests cover every R-4 scenario.

C-6.VerificationIntent: Deterministic gates: tests/renderer/components/tabs-scroll.test.js (pure helper branches + component integration with stubbed geometry) plus the full renderer suite. Manual QA scenario C-6 in the QA document: cycle Ctrl+Tab past the visible edge and confirm the strip follows the active tab.
